scope: Ordinary deterministic staging falsifier; no new unusual experiment and no EntityOS runtime execution.

grf.hypothesis: Archiving the resolved Git tree object with fixed --mtime and gzip -n removes commit-PAX and checkout-metadata variability, making the staged payload byte-reproducible for an equal head/tree.
grf.strongest_counter_reality: Some archive input, attribute/configuration surface, archive backend behavior, or repeated-build environment state remains variable even when head/tree and the visible command arguments are equal.
grf.discriminator: Compare the raw tar and gzip digests from two Vercel build invocations for the exact same head/tree before any Sandbox execution.
grf.observed_outcome: Both the raw tar digest and compressed archive digest/size changed. Therefore gzip metadata is not the sole cause; nondeterminism exists at or before raw tar construction.

external_primary_evidence.finding: Git documents --mtime as the archive-entry modification-time override and documents the commit-id global PAX header for tar archives of commit/tag objects. V4 archives a tree object and supplies --mtime, so the observed raw-tar drift must not be explained away as expected commit-PAX behavior without further evidence.

ordinary_next_discriminator.purpose: Run the same git archive operation twice inside one build invocation, compare again across the repeated Vercel build-hook invocation, and record the first differing byte/header plus Git version, umask, tar.* config and export-subst paths.

parallel_frontier.interpretation: The highest-value shared blocker is reproducible credential-free source/provenance attestation rather than source payload determinism alone.

next_falsifier: Resolve a reproducible credential-free attestation mechanism and then run one fresh exact-head isolated Vercel Sandbox rebuild/execute of the then-current EntityOS candidate with current provenance/security gates.
